children: German satellite maker OHB has been awarded a contract worth nearly 1 billion euros ($1.16 billion) from European satellite operator SES to develop and produce 18 satellite platforms.

The new satellite platforms will be used for the IRIS2 Secure Connectivity Programme--a European Union project designed to provide sovereign, high-speed, and encrypted satellite communication capabilities.
The IRIS2 system will comprise a constellation of 348 satellites operating in low and medium-Earth orbit.
SES is leading the delivery of the medium-Earth orbit segment of IRIS2 as part of a consortium known as SpaceRISE that includes Eutelsat and Hispasat.
OHB said the launch of the first satellites under the contract is planned for 2029, with initial services expected to become available in 2030.
